study type: Individual matched study nested within a prospective cohort
exposure: Infants born outside a level-3 centre (outborn)
Infants born in a level-3 centre (inborn)
outcome: Moderate-to-severe neurological impairment at 5.5 years of age
cohort: 498 outborn and 1235 inborn infants born between 24 and 31 weeks gestation and followed up to 5.5 years of age
finding: There was no difference in survival without moderate-to-severe neurodevelopmental impairment to 5.5 years of age between inborn and outborn very preterm children when matched for gestational age and antenatal steroids.
mod_finding: Caesarian birth was more frequent among inborns, while spontaneous labor was more frequent among outborns.
